name: vinagre de caña o de coco
issue: No key; coconut vinegar is a coconut source (and a coconut-aminos swap for soy adds more).

name: helado de vainilla
issue: Keyed 'cream' (milk only). Most vanilla ice cream is custard-based (egg yolk) and many contain stabilizers/emulsifiers from soy or corn; cream's subs (coconut cream, cashew cream) don't work as an ice-cream swap.
suggest: milk, egg; check label for soy/corn; consider dedicated icecream key with dairy-free ice cream sub

name: licor de avellana o amaretto
issue: No key; liqueur is alcohol. Hazelnut liqueur is tree nut; amaretto is almond/apricot-kernel flavored.

name: rábano picante
issue: Keyed 'mustard' but horseradish is not mustard; mustard-allergic users would be told to swap it for honey (wrong), while prepared horseradish is untracked. Prepared horseradish often contains sulphites; creamed versions contain milk/egg.
suggest: new horseradish key (sulphite; check label for milk/egg); do not key as mustard

name: vinagre de manzana
issue: No key; cider vinegar can carry sulphites.

name: mayonesa
issue: Store-bought mayo is often made with soybean oil and many brands (esp. European) contain mustard; key only covers egg.

name: polvo de hornear
issue: No key; baking powder typically contains cornstarch (some contain wheat starch).

name: coñac
issue: No key; brandy is alcohol and a sulphite source.

name: Alfajores
issue: Tip says to store them in a tin with a slice of bread; for a gluten-free version the bread transfers wheat. Tip should say gluten-free bread (or omit bread).
suggest: reword tip: 'a slice of bread (gluten-free if needed)'

name: dulce de leche
issue: Keyed condensedmilk (milk, sugar) - OK for milk, but commercial dulce de leche may contain corn syrup/glucose and baking soda; coconut condensed milk sub will not set as thick filling.
suggest: milk, sugar; check label for corn

name: fettuccine frescos
issue: Keyed 'pasta' (wheat only). Fresh fettuccine is normally egg pasta.

name: espaldilla de cerdo
issue: No key on the main protein: pork is not flagged at all.

name: pasta de achiote
issue: No key; commercial achiote paste usually contains vinegar and often corn or wheat flour as filler.
suggest: sulphite, corn; check label for wheat

name: vinagre blanco
issue: No key; distilled white vinegar in the US is usually corn-derived.

name: extracto de almendra amarga
issue: No key; bitter almond extract is from bitter almonds/apricot kernels, a tree-nut concern (and usually alcohol-based).

name: azúcar glas
issue: icingsugar key tracks sugar only; powdered sugar usually contains cornstarch.

name: avena en hojuelas
issue: No key; oats are usually cross-contaminated with wheat unless certified gluten-free. A wheat-free swap of the flour alone leaves gluten in the biscuit.
suggest: wheat/gluten (unless certified GF oats); add oats key

name: jarabe dorado
issue: Keyed 'molasses'; a dedicated 'goldensyrup' key exists and is the correct one (same allergen tags, but the sub note talks about molasses bitterness).

name: risotto frío
issue: No key; risotto is normally made with butter, parmesan, stock (celery) and white wine.
suggest: milk, celery, alcohol, sulphite; check stock label for wheat/soy

name: ragú espeso
issue: Keyed 'tomato' only. Ragù contains meat (often pork), soffritto with celery, wine, and often milk.
suggest: nightshade, celery, alcohol, sulphite, milk; pork if pork is used

name: huevos
issue: Egg role is 'binder', so a flax-egg sub is offered, but step 5 also uses beaten egg as the breading wash; flax egg does not work as a dredge.
suggest: add egg-wash sub note (e.g. flour-and-water slurry or plant milk) for the breading step

name: caldo de pollo
issue: No key; store-bought stock commonly contains celery and may contain wheat, soy or yeast extract.
suggest: celery; check label for wheat, soy

name: huevos
issue: Egg role 'enrich' offers cornstarch + plant milk, but steps/tips say 'must never boil' and 'if it boils it curdles'; a cornstarch-thickened version must come to a simmer to thicken. Also 'the eggs are now tempered and safe' does not apply.
suggest: flag steps 3-5 and tip 1 as egg-only; add note for the cornstarch swap (corn)

name: chocolate negro
issue: darkchocolate key tracks soy only; many dark chocolates contain milk (milk fat) or carry a may-contain-milk warning.

name: azúcar glas
issue: icingsugar key tracks sugar only; powdered sugar usually contains cornstarch.

name: Baccalà Mantecato
issue: Step 6 says serve on toasted bread, but bread is not in the ingredient list, so wheat is never flagged for this dish.
suggest: add bread ingredient (k=bread) or mark as optional with wheat

name: bacalao salado
issue: Fish is the whole emulsion (steps 4-5 and tips rely on fish gelatin); the whitefish subs (king oyster/hearts of palm/tofu) will not emulsify, so the steps are misleading for a fish-free version.
suggest: mark as no practical substitute, or add a note

name: extracto de vainilla
issue: No key; pure vanilla extract is about 35% alcohol.

name: chocolate negro
issue: darkchocolate key tracks soy only; many dark chocolates contain milk or may-contain milk.

name: verduras crudas
issue: No key; the crudités list explicitly includes celery (apio) plus bell pepper (nightshade).

name: avena en hojuelas
issue: No key; oats are gluten-contaminated unless certified gluten-free.
suggest: wheat/gluten unless certified GF; add oats key

name: polvo de hornear
issue: No key; baking powder typically contains cornstarch.

name: extracto de vainilla
issue: No key; vanilla extract is ~35% alcohol.

name: chocolate negro
issue: darkchocolate key tracks soy only; many dark chocolates contain or may contain milk.

name: masa quebrada dulce
issue: Keyed 'apflour' (wheat only). Sweet shortcrust is made with butter and usually egg yolk.

name: extracto de almendra
issue: No key; almond extract is from bitter almond/apricot kernel oil and alcohol-based.

name: azúcar glas
issue: icingsugar key tracks sugar only; powdered sugar usually contains cornstarch.

name: extracto de vainilla
issue: No key; vanilla extract is ~35% alcohol.

name: chocolate negro
issue: darkchocolate key tracks soy only; many dark chocolates contain or may contain milk.

name: polvo de hornear
issue: No key; baking powder typically contains cornstarch.

name: coco rallado
issue: Keyed correctly (coconut), but the coconut sub (toasted ground oats) contains gluten unless certified GF oats; worth a note on the desiccatedcoconut sub.
suggest: sub note: use certified GF oats (wheat)

name: kétchup
issue: Keyed 'tomato' only. Ketchup contains vinegar (often corn-derived), often high-fructose corn syrup, and sometimes celery/'natural flavors'.
suggest: nightshade, sugar, corn; check label for celery

name: vinagre de manzana
issue: No key; cider vinegar can carry sulphites.

name: salsa Worcestershire
issue: Keyed 'anchovy' (fish only). Worcestershire contains malt vinegar (barley/gluten) and often soy/sulphites; the anchovy sub (capers or miso) is also not a Worcestershire substitute.
suggest: fish, wheat/gluten, sulphite; check soy; add worcestershire key

name: vinagre de estragón
issue: No key; tarragon vinegar is usually wine-vinegar based.

name: yemas de huevo
issue: Egg yolks are the whole emulsion; eggyolk subs (cornstarch slurry or aquafaba) won't hold a warm béarnaise, and steps 3-4 and tip 3 (triple over steaming water, never above 55 °C) only apply to real yolk.
suggest: add note: no reliable egg-free swap for this sauce

name: vinagre de vino blanco
issue: No key; wine vinegar contains sulphites.

name: mantequilla fría
issue: Butter is the whole sauce; vegan block butter will not emulsify the same way and the rescue tip uses dairy cream. Flag for dairy-free users that the technique notes assume dairy.

name: vinagre de manzana
issue: No key; cider vinegar can carry sulphites.

name: masala de biryani
issue: No key; commercial spice blends can contain mustard, celery seed or asafoetida cut with wheat flour, and are often packed in facilities with peanut/tree nuts.

name: pasta de jengibre y ajo
issue: Keyed 'garlic' only; ginger is untracked (not a listed allergen, informational) and jarred pastes may contain preservatives/sulphites.
suggest: allium; check jarred paste label for sulphite

name: polvo de hornear
issue: No key; baking powder typically contains cornstarch.

name: extracto de vainilla
issue: No key; vanilla extract is ~35% alcohol.

name: amaretti
issue: Keyed 'almondflour' but these are amaretti cookies: almond/apricot kernel plus egg white and sugar (some brands contain wheat). Egg is untracked, and the almond-flour sub (sunflower flour) is not a sensible swap for crushed cookies.
suggest: treenut, egg, sugar (check wheat); new amaretti key with a nut-free crushed-cookie sub

name: ron o marsala
issue: No key; rum/marsala is alcohol (marsala also sulphites), and it's added unbaked into a gently baked custard so the alcohol largely stays.

name: vinagre de vino tinto
issue: No key; wine vinegar contains sulphites.

name: Brasato al Barolo
issue: Blurb says the wine reduces 'until all its alcohol is gone'. A 3-hour covered braise still retains some alcohol (roughly 5-10%); misleading for people avoiding alcohol.
suggest: reword blurb: 'until most of the alcohol cooks off'; keep alcohol tag

name: vino tinto
issue: Keyed winered, OK. Note the wine sub (stock + vinegar) brings in stock (celery, possibly wheat/soy) and wine vinegar (sulphite).
suggest: sub note: stock label check (celery); vinegar sulphite

name: chocolate negro
issue: darkchocolate key tracks soy only; many 70% chocolates contain or may contain milk.

name: extracto de vainilla
issue: No key; vanilla extract is ~35% alcohol.

name: granas de chocolate
issue: Keyed chocolatechips (milk, soy, sugar). Chocolate sprinkles also often contain confectioner's glaze/shellac, corn syrup/starch and colorings; the chocolatechips sub (chopped 70% chocolate) doesn't work as a coating.
